title: Trial balance
examples: What is the main job of a trial balance?
If my trial balance doesn't balance, what does that mean?
Can a trial balance show all the mistakes in my accounts?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the trial balance. It is a list of all the accounts from your ledger. This list helps us check our accounting work. We list every account's balance on one side or the other.

draw.text: Trial Balance: List of account balances

explain.say: The main purpose is to check if the total debits equal the total credits. This confirms the basic mathematical equality of your books. If they match, it suggests the arithmetic is correct.
A simple example is listing Cash, which has a debit balance. You would also list Capital, which usually has a credit balance. We put these balances into the correct columns.

draw.text: Cash: Debit Balance; Capital: Credit Balance

explain.say: These accounts are the balances carried forward from your ledger accounts. You take the final balance from each ledger account. This balance is then transferred to the trial balance sheet.
A real-life example is a small shopkeeper checking his daily sales records. He totals all his cash receipts and all his credit sales. This check ensures his daily books balance out.
A common mistake is forgetting to list a balance from a ledger account. If you miss one, the two totals will not match. Always check every single account balance.

faq.q: What does it mean if my trial balance doesn't balance?
faq.a: It means there is an error in the recording or posting of transactions. It does not mean the business is failing. You must find the mistake.
asks: What does an unbalanced trial balance show?

faq.q: Does a trial balance show every mistake made in the business?
faq.a: No, it only checks the mathematical equality of debits and credits. It will miss certain types of errors. We learn about those specific errors later.
asks: Can I trust the trial balance completely?
What errors does it fail to catch?

faq.q: Do I list the actual transactions or the balances?
faq.a: You must only list the final balances from your ledger accounts. The trial balance summarizes the totals, not the individual entries. Keep the transactions in the journal.
asks: Should I put the journal entries here?
What kind of numbers go on the trial balance?

faq.q: What is the difference between a ledger and a trial balance?
faq.a: The ledger is where you record every transaction in detail. The trial balance is just a summary list of the final totals from that ledger.
asks: Is the trial balance the same as the ledger?
Which one is the main record book?

faq.q: Do I use the same accounts for every period?
faq.a: Most balance sheet accounts remain consistent. However, profit and loss accounts change every accounting period. Always check the required accounts for the period.
asks: Do I include sales revenue every time?

facts: The trial balance lists all ledger account balances.
Its main purpose is to check if total debits equal total credits.
It does not reveal all types of accounting errors.
If it balances, the arithmetic posting is likely correct.

quiz.say: If the total debits are £1000 and total credits are £1000, the trial balance is:
quiz.why: Because the total debits equal the total credits, the basic accounting equation holds true.

wrong.0: This ignores the credit side of the accounting equation.
wrong.1: This ignores the debit side of the accounting equation.
wrong.2: The equality of the totals is the direct conclusion we can draw.

quiz.say: If a business forgets to list the Cash account balance, what will happen?

options.show: The error is too small to notice
options.say: The error is too small to notice

options.show: Only the Cash side is wrong
options.say: Only the Cash side is wrong

quiz.why: Omitting any balance will cause the debit and credit totals to become unequal.

wrong.0: Even a small omission will cause the totals to be unequal.
wrong.2: An imbalance signals a definite mathematical error somewhere.
wrong.3: The error could be in any account listed on either side.

quiz.say: Which of these items belongs on the trial balance?
quiz.why: The trial balance summarizes the final totals from the ledger accounts.

wrong.0: The trial balance only deals with monetary balances, not dates.
wrong.1: Source documents are the original receipts or invoices.
wrong.3: Journal entries are detailed records, not the final summary.
